strengths: Clearly identifies and addresses the 'identity crisis' problem in multi-human text-to-image generation with compelling visual evidence and practical significance
Proposes a well-designed technical solution (DisCo) combining intra-image diversity, group-wise diversity, count accuracy, and quality rewards with principled compositional formulation
Achieves substantial improvements (98.6% UFA vs. 70.8-73.6% baselines, 98.3% GIS) while maintaining competitive perceptual quality
Provides comprehensive experimental validation with rigorous ablation studies (Tables 2, E.2-E.5) and extensive evaluation across multiple metrics and benchmarks
Introduces DiverseHumans benchmark (1,200 curated prompts) with systematic organization by diversity levels, enabling reproducible future research
Demonstrates strong generalization beyond facial identity (clothing diversity, body-type diversity, out-of-distribution people counts) and general text-to-image capability (GenEval2)
Validates technical metrics with human preference study (0.91 correlation, Section E.1.8), confirming automated metrics align with human perception
Excellent reproducibility with detailed algorithms, hyperparameters, implementation details, and commitment to release code/data
weaknesses: Method scope limited to face-based identity relying on face detection (RetinaFace) and facial embeddings, degrading under occlusion, extreme poses, or small faces; no analysis of face detection failure modes

Design choices appear empirically driven with limited principled justification: cosine similarity threshold (0.5) sensitivity unexplored, sigmoid mapping (λ=5) not analyzed, reward weight selection (0.50/0.10/0.15/0.15) grid-based but rationale limited
Limited computational cost analysis despite 13-hour training requirement; cost-benefit tradeoff for practitioners not clearly quantified
Lacks concrete failure case examples and analysis of scenario types where method struggles; no discussion of performance degradation patterns
Metrics limitations: UFA sensitivity to similarity threshold not explored, GIS metric novel but lacks literature comparison, Count Accuracy binary without partial success capturing
User study relatively modest in scale (25 participants, 22 image pairs) though correlation is convincing; no statistical significance testing
Curriculum learning design (Eq. 10) presented as efficient but empirical justification limited; limited exploration of alternative annealing schedules
No analysis of demographic balance or fairness in generated people; limited discussion of potential misuse for generating fake group photos
Training dataset specificity (30,000 curated prompts) with potential distribution shift for out-of-training scenarios not thoroughly discussed

strengths: Identifies and clearly demonstrates an important, previously underexplored problem (identity crisis) affecting multiple SOTA text-to-image models

Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple datasets (DiverseHumans, MultiHuman-TestBench), metrics (Count Accuracy, UFA, GIS, HPS), and baselines with strong quantitative improvements (98.6% UFA vs 85.1% for Krea)
Well-designed compositional reward framework with four complementary components (intra-image diversity, group-wise diversity, count accuracy, quality) that elegantly target different failure modes
Excellent generalization across multiple base models (Flux, Krea, OmniGen, HiDream, Nanobana) and extends beyond facial identity to clothing and body-type diversity
Outstanding reproducibility: detailed algorithms, complete implementation details, hyperparameter specifications, training time/hardware, and public dataset/code release plan
Thorough ablation study (Table 2) demonstrating necessity of all components, and user preference study with 0.91 correlation between metrics and human judgment
Capability to scale beyond training distribution (2-7 people) to 10 individuals while maintaining quality
Maintains general text-to-image capabilities (GenEval2 results) while addressing identity diversity problem
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty beyond reward engineering: the RL framework (Flow-GRFO) is from prior work, and the main contribution is problem-specific reward design rather than algorithmic innovation
Strong dependency on face detection (RetinaFace with confidence threshold 0.7) with degraded performance under occlusion, extreme poses, or small faces; no empirical robustness analysis provided
Training data limited to 30,000 carefully curated prompts in specific social contexts; generalization to culturally diverse or unconventional group compositions not thoroughly evaluated

Evaluation limitations: relatively small user study (25 participants, 22 pairs), UFA metric relies on face embeddings which may not perfectly capture perceptual distinctiveness, main results on 2-7 people with limited exploration of larger groups
Insufficient justification for key design choices: aggregation function selection (Eq. 5), sigmoid temperature (λ=5 in Eq. 6), and weight initialization appear somewhat arbitrary despite grid search
Missing analysis of remaining failure modes and edge cases; no systematic evaluation of when the method fails (similar-looking individuals, very large groups, complex compositions)
Computational cost (13 hours training on 2 H100s) presents barrier to adoption and future research; cost-benefit analysis not discussed
Limited theoretical analysis connecting reward maximization to actual identity distinctiveness; curriculum learning schedule choices lack rigorous justification
No comparison with alternative approaches (e.g., inpainting, sequential generation); ablation on curriculum strategy incomplete
No cross-cultural user study or demographic analysis despite identity perception being culturally sensitive; potential for training distribution bias

strengths: Addresses a genuine and practically important problem in multi-human text-to-image generation with clear motivation (Figure 1)
Strong empirical results: 92.4% Count Accuracy vs 70.8% baseline, 98.6% UFA vs 48.2%, 90.6% GIS vs 50.6%, validated across multiple independent benchmarks
Comprehensive evaluation methodology with multiple complementary metrics and thorough ablation study demonstrating contribution of each component
Well-engineered solution combining flow-GRPO, facial embeddings, and curriculum learning with clear technical presentation and detailed algorithms
Excellent reproducibility efforts with comprehensive implementation details, hyperparameter specifications, and promise to release code and datasets
Extensive qualitative and quantitative results showing consistent improvements across both proprietary and open-source models
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty—primarily an engineering contribution combining established techniques (RL, facial embeddings, curriculum learning) without fundamental methodological innovation
Critical dependency on RetinaFace detection with acknowledged but unanalyzed failure modes (occlusion, extreme poses, small faces), limiting practical applicability and robustness
Insufficient failure mode analysis: Section F is brief; no concrete examples, quantitative failure rates, or analysis of edge cases (identical twins, demographic specifications)
High computational cost (13 hours on 21 H100 GPUs) not adequately addressed; no efficiency comparisons or discussion of optimization potential, limiting accessibility
Limited generalization analysis: training on 30K prompts with 1,200-prompt evaluation set; no systematic study of generalization to different prompt styles, novel models, or demographic variations
Reward function design requires careful manual tuning of multiple hyperparameters with clear sensitivity shown in Table 2; limited guidance for adapting to new models

Metric limitations: facial embedding-based identity metrics unvalidated against human perception; RetinaFace-based metrics inherit detection failures; HPS quality score optimality unclear; human evaluation not extensive
Baseline comparisons against 2023-2025 models, not latest SOTA; limited comparison with specialized identity-aware methods
Curriculum learning strategy uses simple exponential annealing with arbitrary threshold choices; no comparison with alternative curriculum approaches
